prompt: parseDuration in src/duration.js converts an ISO 8601 duration string to a number of seconds, but it only handles hours, minutes and seconds. Extend it to the full form PnYnMnWnDTnHnMnS: years count as 31536000 seconds and months as 2592000 seconds (fixed conversions, no calendar arithmetic), weeks as 604800, days as 86400. The designator M means months before the T separator and minutes after it. A leading minus sign negates the whole duration. The seconds component may be fractional, using either a dot or a comma as the decimal separator, and the result is rounded to three decimal places. Any input that is not a valid ISO 8601 duration, including 'P' with no components and a string with a T separator but no time components, must throw an Error with the message 'invalid duration'. Run `node test/duration.test.js` to check your work.
success_criteria: Year, month, week and day components are parsed
M is months before T and minutes after T
A leading minus sign negates the whole duration
Fractional seconds accept both dot and comma separators
Invalid input throws an Error with the message 'invalid duration'

provenance.incident: Synthetic neutral fixture. Partial ISO 8601 duration support with a hidden verifier covering the date components and the M ambiguity.
